questions.question: What should you do to reduce your chance of an accident?

options.text: Follow the vehicle in front of you as closely as possible.
Do not look ahead and focus only on your controls.
Let other drivers know what you plan to do.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let other drivers know what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, make sure other drivers can see you. Use your signals, brake lights, and lane position to show your intentions. Keep space around your motorcycle and watch the road ahead, behind, and beside you.

questions.question: What happens when you ride alongside another rider?

options.text: You use more of the road.
You have fewer ways to escape if there is a hazard.
You can talk to each other more easily.
Other cars can pass you more easily.

questions.correctAnswerText: You have fewer ways to escape if there is a hazard.
questions.explanation: Do not ride alongside another motorcycle. Doing this limits both of your escape routes if you encounter a hazard.

questions.question: When should you wear reflective clothing?
questions.correctAnswerText: All day and all night.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. Wearing bright and reflective clothing helps other drivers see you at all times.

questions.question: Is braking in a turn easier or harder than braking on a straight road?

options.text: Easier than braking on a straight road.
Harder than braking on a straight road.
Safe if you use only the front brake.
Safe if you use only the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Harder than braking on a straight road.
questions.explanation: Braking in a turn is harder than braking on a straight road. You can use both brakes in a turn, but you must know the correct technique and be very careful.

questions.question: How should a group of riders pass another vehicle?
questions.correctAnswerText: One rider at a time.
questions.explanation: On a two-lane road, riders should pass one at a time. The second rider should wait until the first rider is safely back in the original lane before passing. Continue this pattern until all riders have passed.

questions.question: What is the best way to handle someone tailgating you?

options.text: Move to another lane and let them pass.
Speed up to increase the distance between you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to another lane and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to get them in front of you. If it is safe, change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up may make things worse by causing them to tailgate you at a higher speed.

questions.question: Which colors help riders be seen the best?
questions.correctAnswerText: Orange and red.
questions.explanation: Wear bright orange, red, yellow, or green clothing to be seen by other drivers.

questions.question: What type of shoe soles are best for motorcycle riding?

options.text: Made to let your feet breathe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hard, sturdy, and slip-resistant.
questions.explanation: Wear riding boots or shoes that are high and sturdy to cover and support your ankles. Choose shoes with soles that are hard, sturdy, and slip-resistant.

questions.question: What should you do if the front wheel locks?

options.text: Keep holding the brake until the skid stops.
Release the front brake and never use it again.
Release the front brake and squeeze it again quickly.
Release the front brake right away and apply it smoothly again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake right away and apply it smoothly again.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks, release the front brake completely and right away. Then apply the brake smoothly.

questions.question: What protects your eyes from the wind?
questions.correctAnswerText: Goggles
questions.explanation: Goggles and face shields protect your eyes from wind. Windshields, eyeglasses, and sunglasses do not protect your eyes enough.

questions.question: What is a danger of braking too hard?

options.text: Your wheels lose grip on the road.
You stop before you plan to.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your wheels lose grip on the road.
questions.explanation: When you brake too hard, your wheels can lose grip on the road and you may crash.

questions.question: How long can marijuana affect your driving?
questions.correctAnswerText: More than six hours.
questions.explanation: Smoked marijuana affects you within minutes and can last two to four hours. Eaten marijuana takes over an hour to start working but can last more than six hours.

questions.question: How does a three-wheeled motorcycle handle curves?

options.text: The same as a two-wheeled motorcycle.
It should not be used in curves.
It should use the road shoulder when turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Differently than a two-wheeled motorcycle.
questions.explanation: A three-wheeled motorcycle corners differently than a two-wheeled motorcycle.

questions.question: What sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: If one rider in a group wants to go faster, what should the group do?

options.text: Let the rider go ahead and meet at an agreed place later.
Speed up to keep everyone together.
Let each rider travel at their own speed.
Let the faster rider lead the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the rider go ahead and meet at an agreed place later.
questions.explanation: If one rider wants to go faster than the group, let them go ahead and meet at a place you both agree on.

questions.question: What is the best way to stop quickly?

options.text: Release the throttle and use the front brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, apply both brakes at the same time with firm pressure.

questions.question: When you cannot avoid hitting an object or uneven surface, what should you do?

options.text: Lean the motorcycle to one side.
Rise slightly off the seat so your legs can cushion the impact.

questions.correctAnswerText: Rise slightly off the seat so your legs can cushion the impact.
questions.explanation: If you must ride over an obstacle, slow down as much as possible and keep the motorcycle upright. Rise slightly off the seat so your knees absorb some of the force. Just before impact, gently roll on the throttle to lighten the front wheel.

questions.question: What does eye contact with another driver mean?

options.text: The driver will definitely yield to you.
It is not worth the effort.
It does not guarantee the driver will yield to you.
The driver knows you are there.

questions.correctAnswerText: It does not guarantee the driver will yield to you.
questions.explanation: Never assume eye contact means another driver will give you the right-of-way. They may still fail to yield.

questions.question: What is the best way for a group to ride together while staying close and safe?
questions.correctAnswerText: In a staggered formation.
questions.explanation: A staggered formation keeps riders close together while giving each person enough space to stay safe. Use single-file in curves, turns, or on highways. Never ride side-by-side.

questions.question: When choosing a helmet, it should be all of the following except:

options.text: Made to meet U.S. Department of Transportation standards.

questions.correctAnswerText: Attractive looking.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation standards, fits snugly, and has no defects like cracks or loose padding. How it looks is not important.
